title: Third Word Worships Spiritual Lightness And Beliefs Security

questions.question: In the comparison, what do the two travelers stand for?
questions.answer: One stands for people who obey Allah’s law, and the other stands for people who rebel and follow their own wishes.

questions.question: What does the road in the passage stand for?
questions.answer: It stands for the journey of human life, from the world before this life, through death, and on to the next life.

questions.question: In the comparison, what do the bag and the weapon stand for?
questions.answer: They stand for worship and being mindful of Allah.

questions.question: Why does worship seem heavy at first, but become easy in a deeper way?
questions.answer: It may look like extra effort, but it brings peace, trust, and inner strength.

questions.question: What truth does the worshipper say in prayer that changes how he sees everything?
questions.answer: He believes that only Allah is truly in charge, gives provision, and controls harm and benefit.

questions.question: How does this belief help a person when he is afraid or in trouble?
questions.answer: It helps him turn to Allah, ask Him for help, and trust Him instead of feeling alone.

questions.question: Why does the worshipper feel protected from disasters?
questions.answer: Because he depends on Allah and feels safe under His care.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the root of bravery?
questions.answer: True bravery comes from faith in Allah and worship.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the root of cowardice?
questions.answer: It comes from going astray and living without right guidance.

questions.question: What example is given to show how strong a believing heart can be?
questions.answer: A person with a bright heart would not panic even at something as huge and frightening as the earth blowing apart.

questions.question: How is the fearful philosopher different from the worshipper?
questions.answer: He had worldly learning but lacked a believing heart, so he became terrified by a comet.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about human weakness?
questions.answer: People need many things and face many dangers, but their own strength and resources are very small.

questions.question: If people are so weak, why are worship, Allah’s oneness, trust in Him, and submission so important?
questions.answer: They give the human soul great help, happiness, and support beyond its own weak power.

questions.question: What is one main lesson of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Real peace and courage come from faith, worship, and relying on Allah.

questions.question: Which kind of person is represented by the traveler who submits to the law?
questions.answer: A person who obeys Allah and lives by His commands.

questions.question: Which kind of person is represented by the rebellious traveler?
questions.answer: A person who goes against Allah’s way and follows personal desires.

questions.question: What stages are included in the road of life in this passage?
questions.answer: It begins before worldly life, passes through the grave, and continues to the hereafter.

questions.question: What two religious duties are pictured as the travel gear?
questions.answer: Worship and fear of Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the outside and inside of worship?
questions.answer: On the outside it may seem difficult, but inside it holds great ease and comfort.

questions.question: During prayer, what belief opens a person to Allah’s mercy?
questions.answer: Believing that no one besides Allah truly creates and provides.

questions.question: What does the worshipper understand about good and harm?
questions.answer: He knows both are under Allah’s control.

questions.question: How does knowing Allah is wise and merciful affect the worshipper?
questions.answer: It helps him trust that Allah’s actions have wisdom and that His kindness is great.

questions.question: What does the worshipper do after understanding these truths?
questions.answer: He makes dua, seeks shelter with Allah, and depends on Him.

questions.question: What kind of feeling grows in the worshipper because of this trust?
questions.answer: Strong confidence and calmness grow in him.

questions.question: How does the passage connect faith and courage?
questions.answer: It says courage grows from belief and worship.

questions.question: How does the passage connect misguidance and fearfulness?
questions.answer: It says being far from true guidance leads to cowardice.

questions.question: Why is the story of the comet included?
questions.answer: To show that a person without a believing heart can be scared easily, even if he seems smart.

questions.question: What contrast is made between the philosopher’s mind and heart?
questions.answer: He was called enlightened in his thinking, but his heart was empty of faith.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the limits of human power?
questions.answer: A person can only do a little by himself, even though his needs and worries are huge.

questions.question: What final conclusion does the passage make about worship and trusting Allah?
questions.answer: They are a great blessing and source of happiness for weak and needy human beings.

questions.question: What is the main comparison used at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: It compares two travelers to two kinds of people in real life.

questions.question: What makes the two travelers different from each other?
questions.answer: One obeys divine guidance, while the other follows his own desires.

questions.question: What does the road symbolize besides daily life?
questions.answer: It symbolizes the full journey of the soul through life, death, and the next world.

questions.question: Why are worship and fear of Allah compared to things a traveler carries?
questions.answer: Because they may feel like responsibilities, but they help and protect a person on the journey.

questions.question: What statement from prayer is especially important in the passage?
questions.answer: The statement that only Allah deserves worship.

questions.question: How does this statement change the way a believer looks at the world?
questions.answer: He sees signs of Allah’s mercy everywhere and knows everything is under Allah’s rule.

questions.question: What does the worshipper understand about Allah as Provider?
questions.answer: He understands that all provision comes from Allah alone.

questions.question: When the worshipper faces danger, what three things does he do?
questions.answer: He asks Allah for help, takes refuge in Him, and trusts Him.

questions.question: What result comes from this trust in Allah?
questions.answer: The person becomes stronger inside and less shaken by troubles.

questions.question: Which quality is linked with true goodness in the passage?
questions.answer: Courage.

questions.question: Which quality is linked with sin and wrong guidance?
questions.answer: Cowardice.

questions.question: What extreme picture is used to show a believer’s calmness?
questions.answer: Even a massive disaster would not make him lose himself in fear.

questions.question: What does the example of the comet show about a faithless heart?
questions.answer: It can become frightened very quickly, even over something far away.

questions.question: What does the passage say about human needs compared with human ability?
questions.answer: Human needs are countless, but human ability is tiny.

questions.question: How far can human hopes and worries reach, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They can stretch as far as a person can see and imagine.

questions.question: Based on the passage, why is reliance on Allah reasonable for people?
questions.answer: Because people are weak and needy, so they need Allah’s support more than their own limited power.

questions.question: In this passage, what kind of person follows divine law?
questions.answer: A person who submits to Allah’s guidance.

questions.question: In this passage, what kind of person follows personal desires?
questions.answer: A rebellious person who chooses his own way instead of Allah’s way.

questions.question: What larger journey does the road of life point to?
questions.answer: It points to the journey from the unseen beginning, through the grave, to the hereafter.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the traveler’s supplies in the comparison?
questions.answer: They mean acts of worship and being conscious of Allah.

questions.question: What deeper gift does worship bring that makes it easier than it seems?
questions.answer: It brings inner relief, trust, and spiritual lightness.

questions.question: What belief helps the worshipper find mercy in everything?
questions.answer: The belief that Allah alone creates, provides, and controls all matters.

questions.question: What does the worshipper learn about Allah’s actions?
questions.answer: He learns that Allah acts with wisdom and mercy, never without purpose.

questions.question: How does the worshipper respond after learning this?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah in dua and depends on Him.

questions.question: What does it mean that everything is under the command of the worshipper’s Lord?
questions.answer: It means all creation is controlled by Allah, not by chance or independent power.

questions.question: How does that belief affect the worshipper’s feelings during hard times?
questions.answer: It gives him confidence and helps him not be crushed by fear.

questions.question: What produces real courage in a person?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah together with worship.

questions.question: What produces cowardice in a person?
questions.answer: Misguidance and wrongdoing.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by comparing the believer and the frightened philosopher?
questions.answer: Faith gives calmness, while a heart without faith can stay fearful even if a person seems educated.

questions.question: Why does the passage say humans especially need Allah?
questions.answer: Because they face endless needs and troubles with very little strength of their own.

questions.question: What four things are named at the end as great blessings for the human spirit?
questions.answer: Worship, believing in Allah’s oneness, trusting Him, and submitting to Him.

questions.question: Who does the obedient traveler represent in the passage?
questions.answer: He represents people who accept and follow Allah’s law.

questions.question: Who does the rebellious traveler represent?
questions.answer: He represents people who resist guidance and chase their own desires.

questions.question: What does the road include after a person dies?
questions.answer: It continues through the grave and then to the life to come.

questions.question: What do the carried items teach us about religious duties?
questions.answer: They teach that religious duties may seem like a load, but they actually help us.

questions.question: What key belief is spoken in prayer according to the passage?
questions.answer: The worshipper testifies that only Allah is worthy of worship.

questions.question: How does that belief lead to hope instead of sadness?
questions.answer: It helps the person see Allah’s mercy and kindness all around him.

questions.question: What does the worshipper believe about who controls provision?
questions.answer: He believes Allah alone gives provision.

questions.question: What does the worshipper believe about who controls harm and benefit?
questions.answer: He believes both are in Allah’s hand.

questions.question: Why is it important that Allah is wise and compassionate?
questions.answer: Because it means His actions have purpose and are full of mercy.

questions.question: What actions show that the worshipper relies on Allah?
questions.answer: He prays to Allah, seeks safety with Him, and puts his trust in Him.

questions.question: What is the result of this reliance when trouble comes?
questions.answer: The person gains protection in his heart and becomes confident.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relationship between belief and bravery?
questions.answer: It says belief and worship are where bravery comes from.

questions.question: What does the passage say causes fearfulness and weakness of heart?
questions.answer: Straying from guidance and doing wrong.

questions.question: What is the point of the example about the earth and the comet?
questions.answer: It shows the huge difference between the calm of faith and the panic of unbelief.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about human limits?
questions.answer: Humans can only reach a little by themselves, even though their needs and worries are far greater.

questions.question: What overall benefit does the passage give for worship and trusting Allah?
questions.answer: They bring profit, happiness, strength, and peace to the human soul.

questions.question: What two groups of people are shown through the two travelers?
questions.answer: Those who obey Allah’s law and those who rebel and follow their desires.

questions.question: What does the journey path stand for in human life?
questions.answer: It stands for the full path of life leading through death to the hereafter.

questions.question: What religious meanings are given to the traveler’s equipment?
questions.answer: The equipment stands for worship and fear of Allah.

questions.question: What surprising truth does the passage teach about worship?
questions.answer: Even if it looks heavy, it carries a deep ease that is hard to describe.

questions.question: What does the worshipper say in prayer that strengthens his faith?
questions.answer: He bears witness that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: How does this belief help the worshipper understand the world?
questions.answer: He understands that Allah alone creates, provides, and rules all things.

questions.question: What does the worshipper know about events that happen in life?
questions.answer: He knows they happen under Allah’s wise and merciful care.

questions.question: What does taking refuge in Allah mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means turning to Allah for safety because everything is under His command.

questions.question: How does trust in Allah affect the worshipper during disasters?
questions.answer: It makes him firm and gives him full confidence.

questions.question: What is named as the source of true courage?
questions.answer: Faith in Allah and worship.

questions.question: What is named as the source of cowardice?
questions.answer: Misguidance.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast a heart full of faith with a mind that only seems bright?
questions.answer: A faithful heart stays calm, while a person with only outward cleverness can still be full of fear.

questions.question: What example shows this contrast clearly?
questions.answer: The believer stays unafraid in a huge imagined disaster, but the philosopher panics over a comet.

questions.question: Why is the human spirit described as weak and needy?
questions.answer: Because people need countless things and face many troubles with very little power or resources.

questions.question: What should a thoughtful person understand from all this?
questions.answer: He should understand that worship, belief in Allah’s oneness, trust in Him, and submission to Him are great blessings for human life.
